messages:
incident-bot: Pager: KV_CACHE_SURGE detected in prod us-west-2 (severity: P1). Alert rule: kv.cache.evictions_rate > 3000/s for 60s.
incident-bot: Top symptom: continuous-batching backlog + rope long-context prefetch spikes. Affected services: inference-rope, ntk-prefetch, yarn-window-router.
sam: I’m oncall. looking at graphs now. p50 token latency doubled on inference-rope hosts.
anya: seeing KV cardinality jump 6.8x across the ntk pool. cache hit-rate collapsed to 12%.
mike: customer-facing errors: 502/504 on generation endpoints for ~120 tenants. not all; mostly large-context nets.
jess: any recent deploys?
sam: yes — deploy from 1h ago: yarn/ntk prefetch window increased to 4096 to improve long-span quality. suspect that.
lee: logs from one host: 
```
KV: evict_count=4382 rate=73/s cache_entries=1.2M active_prefixes=240k
continuous-batcher: pending_batches=820 queuesize=62k avg_batch_tokens=2800
rope: mem_pressure=0.87 kv_cache_miss_ratio=0.88
```
lee: heap + GPU memory contended, swap churn on a few nodes.
anya: impact matrix:
- latency up for long-context routes (p95 -> 3.2s)
- increased token cost due to re-fetching prefixes
- some tenants hitting 5xx from gateway timeouts
sam: immediate mitigation ideas: 1) throttle long-context routing, 2) revert prefetch window to previous value, 3) hotpatch continuous-batch config to cap tokens.
mike: prioritize customer-facing fixes first — throttle and circuit-breaker to avoid 5xx.
jess: I can open a status update once we have ETA on rollback/hotpatch.
anya: starting with a cheap routing change: adding a temporary rule to route requests with >2048 tokens to the slow lane (lower concurrency, drop non-critical requests). applying now.
(2m later)
anya: routing change deployed via console. rule id: tmp-longctx-throttle-242888. verifying.
sam: confirming decreased ingress to ntk pool by ~48%. evictions rate down to 1800/s. nice.
lee: still seeing high pending_batches on continuous-batcher, but trending down.
anya: next step: hotpatch to reduce CONT_BATCH_MAX_TOKENS from 8192 -> 2048 on ntk and yarn. This should shrink avg_batch_tokens. prepping patch.
deploy-bot: Starting hotpatch pipeline: hotpatch/cont-batch-cap-242888. CI: ok. 3 nodes in canary.
(6m later)
deploy-bot: Hotpatch applied to canary: cont_batch_max_tokens=2048; observing metrics.
sam: canary looks good. batch avg_tokens down 60%. no increase in user-facing errors. proceeding to rollout.
deploy-bot: Rolling out to 60% -> 100%. Patch complete.
anya: after rollout: pending_batches dropped to ~120, evict_rate stabilized ~420/s, hit-rate up to 58%.
mike: customer impact: 502s reduced by 92% in last 10 minutes. sending note to CS.
customersupport-bot: Drafting customer message: "We experienced elevated errors for long-context requests; temporary throttling and backend configuration hotpatch have been applied; services are stabilizing; we will follow up with root cause and timeline." Anyone want to add details?
jess: add that we reverted a prefetch window increase and limited continuous batch token cap to reduce memory pressure. do not call out internal flags.
customersupport-bot: Updated message. Sending to affected tenants list.
sam: next: safe revert of the prefetch window change. propose revert to previous value 2048, then schedule controlled experiment for long-context quality vs cost.
anya: I’ll open a rollback PR for the prefetch change and coordinate a canary.
lee: ops note: we should also add an emergency circuit-breaker to kv client that rejects requests when per-host eviction_rate > 2000/s to prevent blast radius.
mike: +1. that would protect customers.
(20m later)
anya: rollback PR merged; canary rollback started (nodes: ntk-canary-2).
deploy-bot: Canary rollback completed; metrics look good. proceeding to full rollout.
(5m later)
deploy-bot: Full rollback finished. prefetch_window set to 2048 across ntk and yarn.
anya: final metrics: p50 token latency back near baseline, p95 improved, cache hit-rate restored ~64%, evictions sub-300/s.
sam: closing pager in 30m unless we see regression. great triage.
jess: I’ll log incident and schedule postmortem with SRE + runtime + ML infra. owners: anya (lead), lee (ops), mike (customer comms).
mike: notified design/security for any customer escalations.
lee: follow-up action items:
- add kv client circuit-breaker (owner: lee)
- automated alert for continuous-batcher pending_batches > 500 (owner: anya)
- bake long-context load tests into canary pipeline (owner: sam)
- quantify cost/quality tradeoff for prefetch window sizes (owner: runtime team)
- postmortem doc + timeline (owner: jess)

sam: handoff to next oncall at 03:45 UTC — @anya you have it.
anya: taking over. leaving thread notes and dashboards pinned. :white_check_mark:
customersupport-bot: Sent status update to affected tenants. Responses minimal; one enterprise account opened a ticket, CS engaged.
incident-bot: Pager resolved (auto): KV_CACHE_SURGE no longer firing for 15m.
sam: thanks team — please capture the rollback + hotpatch commands used in the postmortem.
lee: commands for postmortem:
```
# throttle rule
redwood route update --id tmp-longctx-throttle-242888 --max-tokens 2048 --concurrency 2

# hotpatch cont-batch cap
redwood deploy hotpatch cont-batch-cap --env prod --set CONT_BATCH_MAX_TOKENS=2048

# rollback prefetch
git revert <commit-hash-prefetch-window>
redwood deploy --env prod --service ntk --image <previous>
```
jess: noted. I’ll create the incident doc and include timeline + diff graphs.
anya: leaving small note: investigate why kv cache eviction threshold didn't trigger circuit-breaker earlier.
sam: good catch. we will track that in postmortem. closing thread. :lock:
